extracted.intended_audience: adult writers and prospective students interested in Stanford Continuing Studies creative writing courses
extracted.subtask_description: A listing and description of Stanford Continuing Studies creative writing courses and programs (online and on-campus), including genre offerings, formats, instructor qualifications, enrollment rules, and certificate eligibility. Intended to help adult learners choose and register for workshops, generative classes, and certificate-track courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre coverage / course variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Stanford Continuing Studies offers courses and workshops every quarter in the principal genres of writing—novel, short story, poetry, creative nonfiction, and screenwriting. Specialty workshops in travel, memoir, humor, children's literature, and other genres are offered on a rotating basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for courses across these principal genres and rotating specialty topics when selecting a class; the program supports a broad range of genre interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: All Creative Writing courses are taught by experienced authors and teachers, most of whom have been Stegner Fellows in Stanford's Creative Writing program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructor experience (published authors, fellowship background) is presented as a key quality marker; expect instructor-led feedback and craft guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites / accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers at all levels of experience are welcome to join, and most courses have no prerequisites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courses are generally open to beginners through advanced writers; check individual course listings for any exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course formats and delivery modalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses are offered On-Campus, Live Online, Flex Online and other formats (listed in the course table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose format based on location and scheduling needs; format affects how content and feedback are delivered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online format flexibility and access
rubrics_metrics.description: The flexibility of the online format makes it easy to take Continuing Studies Creative Writing courses taught by instructors from Stanford's writing community. You can log into our classes from any computer with Internet access, anywhere and at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online courses are asynchronous/accessible across time zones—suitable for geographically dispersed students or those needing schedule flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online course content components
rubrics_metrics.description: Our online creative writing courses are presented in a clear, straightforward format and contain the elements you look for in a live class, including writing lessons and exercises, as well as feedback from an experienced instructor and fellow students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect online classes to replicate core pedagogical elements of in-person workshops: structured lessons, exercises, and both instructor and peer feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class size and individual attention
rubrics_metrics.description: We keep class sizes small to ensure you get the individual attention you need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small enrollment is framed as a quality control—smaller classes mean more individualized feedback; register early because spots are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience and course suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses are open to all adults, and we encourage all levels of writers to enroll. Whether you are just starting to write, or finishing up your novel, you will find a course suited to your level of experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting a course, align class level and focus (e.g., generative vs. manuscript workshop) with your current stage of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer community and diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will benefit from sharing their work with an eclectic community of writers—writers from many locations, with diverse backgrounds and writing styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer feedback and a diverse cohort are emphasized as pedagogical benefits; consider community fit when choosing a class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration timing and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration opens May 18 8:30 am (PT) (example dates listed). With limited spots available, classes fill quickly. So we encourage you to register today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor registration open dates and act quickly for high-demand courses; some courses may be closed or have wait lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate program eligibility and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: ONLINE CERTIFICATE PROGRAM IN NOVEL WRITING: These courses are only available to students who have been admitted to the Online Certificate Program in Novel Writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain courses are restricted to admitted certificate students—verify eligibility before attempting to enroll in certificate-only offerings.
